input.quote: In each case where one Party shall Manufacture Product for the other Party for clinical use or commercial use, (with the cost and expense of the commercial supply of Product for the U.S. being subject to Section 9.4), the Parties shall negotiate in good faith to enter into a supply agreement (a "Supply Agreement") and a quality agreement (a "Quality Agreement") for such Manufacture on commercially reasonable terms.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay obligation, shortfall penalty or volume cap on Sanofi, so it sits at the preferred position. Searches for "minimum", "shortfall", "commit to purchase" and "purchase" return no such obligation. Article VII (Manufacturing and Supply) leaves clinical/commercial supply terms to a Supply Agreement to be negotiated in good faith on commercially reasonable terms (§7.3) with no committed volumes; §8.2 expressly makes Sanofi's sales and marketing forecasts and net sales projections "non-binding" (p0370, p0371); and §8.3 lets Sanofi appoint distributors in its sole discretion. The payment obligations in Article IX are event-driven (upfront, milestones capped at $520M, royalties on Net Sales) and the Research/Development Budget provisions are budget-capped cost reimbursement — none is a take-or-pay. Sanofi's diligence obligation in §5.7 is a Commercially Reasonable Efforts standard rather than a hard minimum volume or spend, which we note but do not treat as a commitment under this rule. No redline required.
